questions.title: States on the Mississippi River
questions.current_disclaimer: The Mississippi's main stem forms all or part of the border of, or flows through, exactly 10 states. Ordered north to south.

questions.title: States Crossed by the Continental Divide
questions.current_disclaimer: The Continental Divide separates Pacific-draining watersheds from Atlantic/Gulf-draining watersheds. In the US, it runs through five contiguous states plus Alaska.

questions.title: States Crossed by the Appalachian Trail
questions.current_disclaimer: The AT passes through 14 states between Springer Mountain (GA) and Mount Katahdin (ME). Ordered south to north.

questions.title: States Crossed by the Pacific Crest Trail
questions.current_disclaimer: The PCT crosses only three states between the Mexican and Canadian borders. Ordered south to north.

questions.title: Most Interstate Highway Mileage
questions.current_disclaimer: Counts centerline miles of designated Interstate routes only (not other freeways). Ordered longest to shortest.

questions.title: Most Public-Use Airports
questions.current_disclaimer: Counts public-use airports (public and private-owned but open to the public) as tallied by the FAA.

questions.title: Most Bridges (by Count)
questions.current_disclaimer: Counts entries in the National Bridge Inventory (spans of at least 20 feet on public roads). Includes both state-owned and locally-owned bridges.

questions.title: Most Named Mountain Peaks
questions.current_disclaimer: Counts of GNIS features with feature class 'Summit' by state. Every named summit is counted regardless of elevation.

questions.title: Most Named Peaks Over 5,000 ft
questions.current_disclaimer: Named summits above 5,000 ft (1,524 m) with recognized names in Peakbagger's state databases. Elevation cutoff is fixed, not prominence-adjusted.

questions.title: Largest Tribal Land Area
questions.current_disclaimer: Total land area of federally recognized American Indian reservations plus off-reservation trust lands within each state's boundaries.

questions.title: Largest Reservoir Storage Capacity
questions.current_disclaimer: Sum of maximum normal storage across all dams in each state as recorded in the National Inventory of Dams. Interstate reservoirs are credited to the state hosting the dam.

questions.title: Most Named Waterfalls
questions.current_disclaimer: Counts of GNIS features classified as 'Falls' by state. Includes all named cascades regardless of drop height.

questions.title: Largest Rangeland (Grassland) Area
questions.current_disclaimer: Non-federal plus federal rangeland acres as classified by NRCS. Rangeland is distinct from cropland and pastureland.

questions.title: Largest Coniferous Forest Area
questions.current_disclaimer: Timberland and other forestland classified by FIA as softwood forest-type groups (pine, fir, spruce, hemlock, cedar, redwood). Alaska's boreal forests are included.

questions.title: Largest Island Area Under State Jurisdiction
questions.current_disclaimer: Total land area of all islands lying within a state's legal boundaries, including inhabited and uninhabited islands in oceans, gulfs, sounds, lakes, and rivers.

questions.title: Most Named Barrier Islands
questions.current_disclaimer: Named barrier islands as inventoried by USGS coastal geology surveys. Excludes barrier spits still attached to the mainland.

questions.title: Most Named Canyons
questions.current_disclaimer: Counts of GNIS features whose names include 'Canyon' by state. Reflects naming convention as much as underlying topography.

questions.title: Longest River Wholly Within Borders
questions.current_disclaimer: Longest single named river whose entire course lies within one state's boundaries. Rivers that cross state lines are excluded.

questions.title: Most Named Plateaus
questions.current_disclaimer: Counts of GNIS features whose names include 'Plateau' or 'Mesa' by state. Reflects Southwestern mesa-country naming density.

questions.title: Most Named Bays
questions.current_disclaimer: Counts of GNIS features classified as 'Bay' by state, including tidal, lake, and river bays.
